<overview>
Anatomy of `sdkcraft.yaml`, the build-time SDK definition that SDKcraft packs
into a `.sdk` artifact. This file is the schema authority for the skill: if a
key is not listed here, it does not exist — do not import snapcraft muscle
memory (there is no `apps:`, `services:`, `daemons:`, or `confinement:` key).
The runtime `sdk.yaml` is generated by SDKcraft; publishers never write it.
</overview>

<file_identity>
- The definition lives at the project root as `sdkcraft.yaml` (or
  `.sdkcraft.yaml`). Hooks live next to it under `hooks/`; SDKcraft enumerates
  them automatically when packing — they are never listed in the YAML.
- SDKcraft lints every hook with ShellCheck at pack time; a ShellCheck error
  blocks `sdkcraft pack`. Hooks in a packed SDK must also carry the exec bit.
- Packed artifacts are named `<NAME>_<ARCH>_<BASE>.sdk`, one per platform.
</file_identity>

<top_level_fields>
| Key | Required | Value |
|-----|----------|-------|
| `name` | yes | Lowercase letters, digits, inner hyphens; ≤40 chars; at least one letter. Reserved: `agent`, `system`, `sketch`, and any name starting with `try-` or `project-`. |
| `platforms` | yes | Build targets; see below. |
| `base` | no | Runtime base: `ubuntu@20.04`, `ubuntu@22.04`, `ubuntu@24.04`, or `ubuntu@26.04`. Omit for SDKs that work on any supported base. |
| `build-base` | when `base` omitted | Base used to build. |
| `version` | no* | SDK version string. Quote numeric-looking values (`version: "1.0"`). |
| `adopt-info` | no* | Name of the part whose `craftctl set version=...` provides the version at build time. *Exactly one of `version` or `adopt-info` — house style is always `adopt-info` + a `VERSION` file (see below). |
| `title` | no | Human-readable title. |
| `summary` | no | One line, ≤78 chars. |
| `description` | no | Free-form, ~100 words max. Reused by the README overview — write it as a plain multiline string, no headings or bullets. |
| `license` | no | License of what the SDK actually installs, not just the packaging. |
| `contact`, `issues`, `source-code`, `website` | no | Publisher metadata. |
| `package-repositories` | no | Extra repositories enabled during the build (craft-archives format). |
| `parts` | no | craft-parts build instructions. Omitted ⇒ SDKcraft supplies `{default-part: {plugin: nil}}`. |
| `plugs`, `slots` | no | Interface endpoints; see below. Only `mount` and `tunnel` support slots. |

Copied verbatim into the runtime `sdk.yaml`: `name`, `base`, `version`,
`title`, `summary`, `description`, `license`, `contact`, `issues`,
`source-code`, `plugs`, `slots`. Everything else controls the build only.
</top_level_fields>

<version_pattern>
House pattern for every generated SDK: `adopt-info: <part>` plus a `VERSION`
file at the repo root, read in the part's `override-pull`:

```yaml
# <name>/sdkcraft.yaml
adopt-info: <part>
parts:
  <part>:
    plugin: nil
    override-pull: |
      VERSION=$(cat "$CRAFT_PROJECT_DIR/VERSION")
      craftctl set version="$VERSION"
```

Never hardcode `version:` in a generated SDK — the `VERSION` file is what
renovate bumps during repo onboarding, so hardcoding the version would force a
YAML rewrite on every upstream release.
</version_pattern>

<platforms>
Three layouts; pick by base and architecture spread:

1. Single base, named-architecture shorthand (key alone means both `build-on`
   and `build-for`):

```yaml
# <name>/sdkcraft.yaml
base: ubuntu@24.04
platforms:
  amd64:
  arm64:
```

2. Multi-base: no `base`/`build-base`; every platform key (or `build-on`/
   `build-for` entry) is a `<BASE>:<ARCH>` pair. CI uploads then use
   `--platform` instead of `--build-for`:

```yaml
# <name>/sdkcraft.yaml
platforms:
  ubuntu@22.04:amd64:
  ubuntu@24.04:amd64:
```

3. Explicit `build-on`/`build-for`, for cross-builds or arch-independent SDKs:

```yaml
# <name>/sdkcraft.yaml
platforms:
  arm64:
    build-on: [amd64]
    build-for: [arm64]
  all:
    build-on: [amd64, arm64, riscv64]
    build-for: all
```

Supported architectures: `amd64`, `arm64`, `armhf`, `i386`, `ppc64el`,
`riscv64`, `s390x`. `build-for: all` is for SDKs shipping no compiled
binaries.
</platforms>

<parts>
Each entry under `parts:` is a standard craft-parts definition (`plugin`,
`source`, `override-pull`/`override-build`/`override-prime`, `organize`,
`prime`, `build-packages`, ...). SDKcraft-specific deltas:

- `stage-packages` and `stage-snaps` are **hard-rejected** at load time; the
  error text points at the `setup-base` hook, which is where apt/snap
  installation belongs (it integrates with the image's apt cache and keeps
  security updates flowing).
- `build-packages`/`build-snaps` ARE allowed (build-container-only tooling
  such as `curl`, `jq`).
- Common plugins in shipped SDKs: `nil` (hook-only or hand-rolled pulls),
  `dump` (unpack an artifact or copy a local dir), `rust`, `npm`, `cmake`,
  `make`. The full craft-parts plugin set is available.
- `$CRAFT_PROJECT_DIR`, `$CRAFT_PART_SRC`, `$CRAFT_PART_INSTALL`, `$CRAFT_PRIME`,
  `$CRAFT_ARCH_BUILD_FOR`, `$CRAFT_PLATFORM`, and `$CRAFT_PROJECT_VERSION` are
  in scope in overrides; `case "$CRAFT_ARCH_BUILD_FOR" in ...` is the standard
  per-arch download switch.
- Build-time → runtime handoff: a part may write small files into
  `$CRAFT_PART_INSTALL` (a `version` or apt `series` marker) that hooks read
  later via `$SDK/<file>` — this is how build-time platform knowledge reaches
  `setup-base`.
</parts>

<interfaces>
Plug and slot values are inline mappings naming the `interface` plus
interface-specific attributes. The set is closed:

| Interface | Plug | Slot | Naming rule |
|-----------|------|------|-------------|
| `camera` | yes | no | Plug must be named `camera` |
| `custom-device` | yes | no | Free name; at least one of `subsystem`/`vendorid`/`productid`; `productid` requires `vendorid` |
| `desktop` | yes | no | Plug must be named `desktop` |
| `gpu` | yes | no | Plug must be named `gpu` |
| `mount` | yes | yes | Free name |
| `ssh-agent` | yes | no | Plug must be named `ssh-agent` (the interface is `ssh-agent` — there is no `ssh` interface) |
| `tunnel` | yes | yes | Free name; auto-connect matches plug and slot by name |

Mount plug attributes: `workshop-target` (required; absolute path inside the
workshop, `$SDK` expands to the SDK's install path; Workshop creates the
directory if missing), `mode` (octal; defaults `0o775`, or `0o755` when
`uid` is 0), `uid`/`gid` (default `1000` when the target is under
`/home/workshop/`, `/project/`, or `/run/user/1000/`; `0` otherwise),
`read-only` (default `false`).

Mount slot attribute: `workshop-source` (required; absolute path inside the
workshop). Unlike a plug's target, Workshop does NOT create it — the
directory must already exist when the connection is established (create it in
`setup-base`, or ship it via `override-prime: mkdir -p ...` when the source
is under `$SDK`). The pack-time interface linter fails when a `$SDK`-rooted
mount path does not exist in the primed tree.

Tunnel attributes: a single `endpoint` on both plug and slot —
`<ADDRESS>/<PROTOCOL>` (either part may stand alone), address is
`<HOST>:<PORT>`, protocol `tcp` (default) or `udp`; Unix domain sockets as an
absolute `<PATH>` (with `$HOME`/`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` expansion) or abstract
`@<STRING>`. Defaults to `localhost/tcp`. Endpoints starting with `[` or `@`
must be quoted in YAML. The port may be omitted on at most one side.

Shorthand: `gpu:` (null value) or `gpu: gpu` normalizes to
`{interface: gpu}` — the full mapping form is house style for clarity.

For which connections happen automatically versus needing `connections:` or
`workshop connect`, load `../use-workshop/references/interfaces.md` — do not
guess the policy.
</interfaces>

<worked_example>
The `uv` reference SDK, showing a source-built part, `organize`/`prime`, a
mount cache plug, and a mount slot shared with other SDKs:

```yaml
# uv/sdkcraft.yaml
name: uv
adopt-info: uv
base: ubuntu@24.04
summary: An extremely fast Python package and project manager
license: Apache-2.0 OR MIT
platforms:
  amd64:
  arm64:
parts:
  uv:
    plugin: rust
    source: .
    override-pull: |
      VERSION=$(cat "$CRAFT_PROJECT_DIR/VERSION")
      craftctl set version="$VERSION"
      git clone --depth 1 --branch "$VERSION" https://github.com/astral-sh/uv.git .
      craftctl default
    organize:
      uv: bin/uv
      uvx: bin/uvx
    prime:
      - bin/uv
      - bin/uvx
plugs:
  cache:
    interface: mount
    workshop-target: /home/workshop/.cache/uv
slots:
  venv:
    interface: mount
    workshop-source: /home/workshop/uv-venv
```
</worked_example>
